test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 26 Oct, 2023)
subject: general
question: Two friends A and B started a business by investing Rs. 1,50,000 and Rs. 2,50,000, respectively. They agreed to distribute their earnings in the same ratio of their investments. After an year, the profit earned was Rs. 6,00,000. Each of them added Rs. 50,000 to their respective profits and invested in a different project. If this project gave an yield of Rs. 4,20,000, then A’s share in the profit is:
solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Ratio of investments A : B = 1,50,000 : 2,50,000 = 3 : 5. Divide profit ₹6,00,000 in 3 : 5 → A = ₹2,25,000 and B = ₹3,75,000. New investment ratio = (2,25,000 + 50,000) : (3,75,000 + 50,000) = 2,75,000 : 4,25,000 = 11 : 17. A’s share in new profit = (11 ÷ 28) × 4,20,000 = 11 × 15,000 = ₹1,65,000. **∴ The correct answer is ₹1,65,000.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** Initial investment A = ₹1,50,000 | Initial investment B = ₹2,50,000 Profit Project 1 = ₹6,00,000 | Profit Project 2 = ₹4,20,000 **Formula Used:** Profit Ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂) [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33d9d1be121d28e3ee0db87700d57f33005086df051a140be693991a05aab716.png] ⇒ Investment Ratio A : B = 1,50,000 : 2,50,000 = 3 : 5 ⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 3 + 5 = 8 units ⇒ 8 units = ₹6,00,000 ⇒ 1 unit = 6,00,000 ÷ 8 = ₹75,000 ⇒ A’s profit share (Project 1) = 3 × 75,000 = ₹2,25,000 ⇒ B’s profit share (Project 1) = 5 × 75,000 = ₹3,75,000 ⇒ A’s investment (Project 2) = 2,25,000 + 50,000 = ₹2,75,000 ⇒ B’s investment (Project 2) = 3,75,000 + 50,000 = ₹4,25,000 ⇒ New Ratio A : B = 2,75,000 : 4,25,000 = 11 : 17 ⇒ Total ratio units (Project 2) = 11 + 17 = 28 units ⇒ A’s share in Project 2 profit = (11 ÷ 28) × 4,20,000 ⇒ A’s share = 11 × 15,000 = ₹1,65,000 **∴ The correct answer is ₹1,65,000.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** Partnership Profit Sharing Rule Profit is always distributed in the ratio of the product of Investment (Capital) and Time: Profit Ratio = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂). Types of Partnership Simple Partnership occurs when all partners invest for the same time period; Compound Partnership occurs when partners invest for different time durations. Working vs Sleeping Partner A working partner manages the business and may receive a salary or extra commission from the profit before the remaining profit is shared according to investment ratios. 57:T116b,
